exampleSentence: The historic document must undoubtedly have been misplaced in the archives.

definition: Put in the wrong place and lost temporarily.
exampleSentence: He could not have misplaced the confidential blueprint intentionally.

definition: Supposed that something is the case on the basis of probability.
exampleSentence: The ancient vessel may well have sunk during the severe gale.

definition: Not explained or taken into consideration.
exampleSentence: A small amount of laboratory equipment remains unaccounted for.

definition: Serving to settle an issue; decisive.
exampleSentence: The forensic team must have found conclusive evidence at the scene.

definition: An opinion or conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information.
exampleSentence: Why the archive vanished remains a matter of conjecture among historians.

definition: The quality of seeming reasonable or probable.
exampleSentence: The forensic evidence lent plausibility to the defense witness's testimony.

definition: An idea that is taken to be true on the basis of probability.
exampleSentence: The detective operated on the presumption that the culprit held keys.

definition: The state or fact of something being likely; probability.
exampleSentence: In all likelihood, the delayed flight must have encountered head winds.

definition: Suppose that something is true without having evidence to confirm it.
exampleSentence: One can surmise that the ancient settlers must have abandoned the fortress in haste.
